messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Okay, so it needs to come down at 4.5 m/s or less. Nothing bigger than a J. Keep apogee below 1,200 m for the waiver. Cheers.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: landing speed is a maximum of 4.5 m/s. Motor class is a maximum of J. Apogee is a maximum of 1,200 m, the waiver. No altitude floor, no wind, no rail and no stage count are given, so I assume one stage, a 1.5 m rail, 2 m/s wind, vertical, sea level, and one parachute.
2. Feasibility: 1,200 m with no drag needs sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 1200) = 153 m/s. A full J on a light rocket will clear that and break the waiver, so an I-class 38 mm motor in a wider airframe is the safer way to stay legal. Looking up a few I motors under the J cap.

2. Feasibility: the I300T is class I, 436.8 N*s, 295.9 N average, 1.47 s burn, 38 mm, with delays of 6, 10 and 14 s. That stays under the J cap. The I200W and I285R only list a 0 s delay, so they would eject at burnout. 437 N*s in a slim rocket can exceed 1,200 m, so the airframe is a 76 mm blue tube, wide enough to add drag while the motor still lifts it.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 1.20 kg, motor included. Thrust-to-weight = 295.9 / (1.20 * 9.81) = 25.1. Rail acceleration (295.9 - 11.8) / 1.20 = 237 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 237 * 1.5) = 26.7 m/s. Descent mass 1.20 - 0.222 = 0.978 kg. At 4.0 m/s and Cd 0.8, area = 2 * 0.978 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 4^2) = 1.22 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 1.22 / 3.1416) = 1.25 m. A 1.40 m chute leaves margin under 4.5 m/s. Burnout at 1.47 s plus a coast of several seconds fits the 10 s delay.
4. Draft: 76 mm blue tube, 0.85 m long, fiberglass ogive, three elliptical birch fins, 38 mm phenolic mount, I300T-10, one 1.40 m chute on motor ejection. Default wind and rail.

4. Check: the simulator gives 1235.7 m. The waiver is 1,200 m, and (1235.7 - 1200) / 1200 = 0.0298, about 3% over. Landing 3.9 m/s is under 4.5. Rail exit 30.1 m/s, thrust-to-weight 21.4, margin 1.22 cal. The chute opens at 11.6 s, just before apogee at 12.13 s. Liftoff mass is 1.41 kg, heavier than my 1.20 kg guess, and it still cleared the waiver. Motor is an I, inside the J cap.
5. Fix: 1235.7 m is the failing value. A later delay would only let it coast higher, so I am adding drag. Nose and body go from 0.076 m to 0.082 m. The margin should stay near 1.22 * 0.076 / 0.082 = 1.13 cal. Motor, fins and chute stay put.

4. Check: the simulator gives 1175.8 m, under the 1,200 m waiver by 1200 - 1175.8 = 24.2 m. Landing is 4.0 m/s, under 4.5. Rail exit 30.0 m/s and thrust-to-weight 20.5 pass. The miss is the margin: 0.99 cal at rail exit and 0.99 cal through the burn, just under 1.0. My 1.13 cal guess was high. The wider tube grew the reference diameter and the fins did not grow with it.
5. Fix: 0.99 cal is what fails. Elliptical fin span goes from 0.08 m to 0.11 m, which is 0.11 / 0.08 = 1.38 times the span and the same factor on fin area. That moves the CP aft. Root chord stays 0.14 m. There is 24.2 m of waiver room, so a little extra fin drag is acceptable. Nothing else changes.

4. Check: the simulator gives 1130.5 m. The waiver headroom is 1200 - 1130.5 = 69.5 m. Landing is 4.1 m/s against 4.5 m/s, so 4.5 - 4.1 = 0.4 m/s of margin. Rail exit 29.5 m/s, thrust-to-weight 20.1, and the margin is 1.73 cal at rail exit and through the burn, above 1.0. The chute opens at 11.6 s, just before apogee at 12.1 s. The motor is the I300T, inside the J limit.
5. Fix: no further change; the waiver, the landing speed and the margin all pass.
6. Uncertainty: 69.5 m under a hard waiver is comfortable only if the build matches this mass. The simulator has the rocket at 1.50 kg. A lighter finish climbs, and this design was already 36 m over the waiver before the tube got wider. Weigh it. The 4.1 m/s landing uses a chute Cd of 0.8; a lazy canopy would land faster, and 4.5 m/s is a tight ceiling. Drift at 2 m/s was 502 m.
messages.content:
An I300T-10 in an 82 mm blue tube, three elliptical birch fins, and a 1.40 m chute.
The simulator gives 1130.5 m, under the 1,200 m waiver, with 1.73 cal of margin and a 4.1 m/s landing.
